title: Turning AI art into shippable game assets for my roguelite card game
author: Tommyruin
selftext:
I'm building AITA: The Dark Domain, a roguelite card game set in the Etruscan underworld, and one of the biggest solo-dev problems has been turning AI-assisted art into actual game-ready assets.

I used PixelLab for a lot of the card and sprite art, but the useful pipeline has not been "generate art and ship it". It has been:

- generate or explore visual directions quickly  
\- when happy with art direction, generate consistent prompts using the same structure to better obtain good consistent output.
- reject most outputs
- crop out bad framing  
\- manual touch up of bits I dont like in aseprite
- resize assets for actual gameplay scale
- assemble atlases and store/marketing variants
- test whether the art still reads once cards, buttons, VFX, and combat text are on top of it
  
I tried the PixelLab aseprite plugin for manual editing of some of the assets, but found that the web dev setup was much better for my use cases (and often quicker). I mainly used the "Create M-XL Image" tool, and then plugged the same image into the "Image to Pixel Art" tool to generate the thumbnail size images for blessings and bosses. The tool was good imo and I was able to get quite far on the free tier, and in a month on the lowest paid tier. My only wish was that it was easier to select sizing of original output generations.

The hardest lesson has been that a cool image is not automatically a useful game asset. It has to survive compression, fit the UI, support the mechanics, and make the card decisions clearer rather than noisier.

The free solo beta is live here:
[https://aitatdd.com/play](https://aitatdd.com/play)

I also have 50 closed beta/co-op codes for people willing to test whether the visuals and gameplay read clearly in practice. If you want one, leave a comment and I'll randomly DM codes. No NDA; blunt feedback and bug reports are welcome.

comments.body: There is too many battles where you dont get some customisation in play, its just big number wins. you need to get that upgrade loop happening fast.

replies.author: Tommyruin
replies.body:
Thanks so much for the feedback!  
  
I'm hopeful with the wide array of blessings available focusing on different strategies (including low value cards "the uprising"), this will become a bit less of a factor in the full release! In my playtests, I definitely find that the early game feels more "big number wins", but as you progress through and get blessings it balances out. 

If you'd like,  I can provide a full beta code to test more. If you are interested let me know :)
